Counterpoint Research published a latest report showing that in the second quarter of 2026, Apple surpassed Samsung to become the largest smartphone brand in the European telecom operator channel, because telecom operator sales performed more steadily than the overall market. Details are as follows.

Apple drives telecom operator sales, outperforming the broader European smartphone market

Counterpoint Research today (the 4th) released a report stating that smartphone sales through telecom operators in Europe in the second quarter of 2026 declined 4% year-on-year, while the open market declined 11%. The report pointed out that overall smartphone sales fell 8%.

Counterpoint said this once again reflects the impact of rising memory costs, and the European low-end smartphone market has been hit particularly hard. The relatively better performance of telecom operator sales is because the channel tends to focus on high-end models and high-end brands such as Apple, and sells them mainly in the form of monthly contract plans.

The report pointed out that Apple's share of smartphone sales through European telecom operators rose from 33% in the second quarter of 2025 to 37% in the second quarter of 2026; over the same period, Samsung fell from 39% to 34%.

However, Chinese brand vivo posted the largest year-on-year growth in telecom operator sales, reaching 90%; Motorola came in second with a growth of 27%.

Jan Stryjak, Associate Director of Counterpoint Research, has the following analysis of the relevant data:

Stryjak added that the telecom operator channel is expected to continue expanding its market share over the "next few quarters," "because the low-end market continues to be affected by the memory crisis." He also mentioned that, compared with telecom operators, independent retailers have stepped up promotional efforts, "which may offset some of the price increase pressure and bring additional stimulus to the open market."
